papers.title: Use of Maraging Steel 1.2709 for Implementing Parts of Pressure Mold Devices with Conformal Cooling System
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present the results of experimental tests and numerical calculations for parts of foundry mold devices made by selective laser melting (SLM). The main aim of this research was to compare the heat conduction efficiency of the conformal and the traditional channel arrangement. The infusion spreader with a conformal channel arrangement and the test material were made with an M2 Concept Laser Cusing machine using 1.2709 steel powder. Temperature changes in the spreaders were compared between conventional and conformal cooling channels using finite element method (FEM) calculations. The position of the so-called “thermal equilibrium isotherm” was determined for both sprue spreaders, which separate the area of the mold with a constant temperature from the zone of cyclic temperature changes. The components of the sprue spreaders in a stress state caused by temperature changes during the operation of the pressure machine were determined using the FEM model. It was found that the cooling system shortened the time of solidification and cooling of the alloy. Based on the analysis of the strength test results and the fracture surface of the samples, the relationship between heat treatment parameters and the strength, hardness, and elongation of the tested material was determined. The sprue spreaders were installed under a pressure machine and tested under production conditions. The use of a sprue spreader with a conformal cooling system shortened the time of a single cycle of the casting machine compared to the conventional solution.

papers.title: Patient‐Specific 3D Bioprinted Models of Developing Human Heart
papers.abstract: The heart is the first organ to develop in the human embryo through a series of complex chronological processes, many of which critically rely on the interplay between cells and the dynamic microenvironment. Tight spatiotemporal regulation of these interactions is key in heart development and diseases. Due to suboptimal experimental models, however, little is known about the role of microenvironmental cues in the heart development. This study investigates the use of 3D bioprinting and perfusion bioreactor technologies to create bioartificial constructs that can serve as high-fidelity models of the developing human heart. Bioprinted hydrogel-based, anatomically accurate models of the human embryonic heart tube (e-HT, day 22) and fetal left ventricle (f-LV, week 33) are perfused and analyzed both computationally and experimentally using ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging. Results demonstrate comparable flow hemodynamic patterns within the 3D space. We demonstrate endothelial cell growth and function within the bioprinted e-HT and f-LV constructs, which varied significantly in varying cardiac geometries and flow. This study introduces the first generation of anatomically accurate, 3D functional models of developing human heart. This platform enables precise tuning of microenvironmental factors, such as flow and geometry, thus allowing the study of normal developmental processes and underlying diseases.

llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on fabrication and perfusion of bioprinted heart models but includes no AI/ML integration, no intelligent process control, and no data-driven decision-making in the bioprinting workflow.

summary_zh.motivation: 缺乏研究心脏发育中微环境因素的高保真模型
summary_zh.method: 使用3D生物打印和灌注生物反应器构建胚胎心脏管和胎儿左心室模型
summary_zh.result: 打印模型表现出与真实心脏相似的流动模式和内皮细胞生长
summary_zh.validation: 通过超声和MRI成像及细胞实验验证

summary_en.motivation: To create high-fidelity in vitro models of the developing human heart for studying microenvironmental cues in cardiogenesis.
summary_en.method: Hydrogel-based 3D bioprinting was used to fabricate anatomically accurate embryonic heart tube and fetal left ventricle models, which were perfused in a bioreactor.
summary_en.result: Bioprinted constructs exhibited comparable flow hemodynamics to native hearts and supported endothelial cell growth that varied with geometry and flow conditions.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation included computational flow analysis, ultrasound imaging, and magnetic resonance imaging, along with in vitro cell assays.
